workload: One public text-only opportunity exchange. Model has no tools.

response.decision: No pilot is warranted at this stage due to insufficient evidence of self-hosted systems with demonstrable, issue-level performance advantages under bounded token costs. The available records do not provide direct comparisons of self-hosted coding systems against alternatives in terms of reliability, cost efficiency, or outcome quality under controlled token budgets. Without issue-level outcome data from self-hosted systems, any claim of merit remains speculative.
response.incumbent: Publicly available open-source harnesses (e.g., those evaluated in Record B) with proven performance on verified SWE-bench issues under common serving conditions represent the strongest existing alternative. These systems are transparent, benchmarked, and have demonstrated up to 44% higher resolution for one model, indicating operational viability.
limitations: No record provides direct evidence of self-hosted coding systems (e.g., self-hosted LLMs or agents) performing better than open-source harnesses on verified issues under token budget constraints.
All performance claims are aggregated or model-level; no issue-level, per-run, or per-task outcome data from self-hosted systems is available.
Token cost accounting in Record D is sensitive to assumptions and does not establish a baseline for self-hosted systems.
Missing usage data in Record C (no imputation) limits reliability of token cost modeling.

opportunities.move: Conduct a targeted analysis of Record B to identify which open-source harnesses achieve the highest resolution on SWE-bench issues with minimal token usage, and propose a pilot using one of those harnesses as a baseline for comparison with self-hosted alternatives in future stages.
opportunities.title: Baseline Performance Analysis of Open-Source Harnesses

opportunities.move: Extract and analyze the per-run token usage and failure labels from Record C to build a public, issue-level benchmark dataset for token cost modeling, enabling future evaluation of self-hosted systems under bounded token allowances.
opportunities.title: Issue-Level Token Cost Benchmarking from Public Run Records

opportunities.move: Formally evaluate whether any of the models in Record A (context management, planning, action space) show consistent performance gains across benchmarks that could be ported to self-hosted agents, with a focus on context window and planning efficiency.
opportunities.title: Model-Level Context and Planning Efficiency Analysis

opportunities.move: Use Record D’s trial acquisition and budget-constrained agent selection framework to model how agent selection under token limits might be optimized—without assuming self-hosted superiority—providing a framework for future pilot design.
opportunities.title: Budget-Constrained Agent Selection Framework

opportunities.move: Propose a pilot of a self-hosted coding system (e.g., a lightweight agent using a public model like Llama 3 or CodeLlama) only if a specific, issue-level performance claim is made with supporting data from Record C or B, and if the claim is independently verifiable via public run logs.
opportunities.title: Conditional Pilot Proposal with Issue-Level Verification

response.test: Smallest discriminating test: For any proposed self-hosted system, demonstrate that it resolves at least one verified SWE-bench issue (from Record C) with a lower per-issue token cost than the best-performing open-source harness (from Record B), and that the outcome is reproducible across at least two independent runs with identical prompts and context.
